Where it began

Yashasvi Jaiswal comes from Suriyawan, in Uttar Pradesh, where he was born on 28 December 2001, the youngest of four. At ten he moved to Mumbai to train at Azad Maidan, and for three years he lived in a tent beside the ground with the groundsmen. It was not a comfortable start, but it put him where the cricket was.

In December 2013 the coach Jwala Singh, who ran an academy in Santacruz, saw what he could do and gave him a place to stay. Two years later the schoolboy made 319 not out and took 13 for 99 in the same Giles Shield game, the best all-round effort Indian schools cricket had seen.

The player

He made his name in junior cricket first, as the leading run-scorer and Player of the Tournament at the 2020 Under-19 World Cup. Before that, in 2019, he had become the youngest player to make a double hundred in List A cricket, with 203 in the Vijay Hazare Trophy at the age of 17.

His Test debut came against West Indies in July 2023, and he marked it with 171 in his first innings and the Player of the Match award. Against England in 2024 he made double hundreds in consecutive Tests, the first of them 209, equalled the record of 12 sixes in a Test innings and became the first player to hit 20 sixes in a series. By October 2026 he had 2,612 runs from 31 Tests at 47.49, with seven hundreds, 13 fifties and a highest score of 214 not out.

What made him special

He likes a big score and, once in, he rarely settles for a small one. He also travels well. He made a hundred in his first Test in the West Indies, in Australia, with 161 at Perth, and in England, with 101 at Leeds. No visiting batter before him had made a century on his first appearance in both England and Australia.

He has bowled a little in Tests without yet taking a wicket. Batters everywhere can enjoy that while it lasts.

Away from the middle

He plays for Rajasthan Royals in the Indian Premier League, and in 2023 he hit the fastest fifty the competition had seen, in 13 balls. He was in the Indian squad that won gold at the Asian Games, and in 2025 Time magazine put him on its Time 100 Next list.

And finally

He began by sleeping in a tent beside a Mumbai maidan and has gone on to make himself at home on Test grounds around the world. Bowlers in the countries he has yet to visit may be hoping for a quieter introduction than the others got.
